text:
The investor's designation of the 10-acre tract was not an easement or a restrictive covenant; it was an offer to dedicate the tract to public use, which the school board accepted by voting to build the school. Since recording the plat and the board's acceptance within a reasonable time made the dedication effective, the closest listed answer is neither option—but if forced between the two, it is best characterized as an easement for public use rather than a restrictive covenant.  
CONFIDENCE: 55
